scope: Document/Save As/autosave/refactoring saves and native settings patches use shared process-local resource locks. No persistent save sidecars or separate lock directory. This is not whole extension API or platform qualification.

source_cohort.selection: git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard; unique existing files, sorted UTF-8 relative paths
source_cohort.digest_algorithm: sha256(concatenate(path UTF-8 + NUL + raw sha256(file bytes)))

source_reference.observation: resourceLocks stores per-resource Barrier instances in memory; disposal removes the entry and opens the barrier. Atomic writes use transient adjacent files.

integrity_evidence: Three new resource-map controls cover same-resource exclusion, independent resources, waiter handoff, canonical parent aliases, panic release and no filesystem artifacts.
Existing save/settings shutdown and coordination controls now inspect the actual shared in-memory guard and require absent sidecars rather than creating or expecting them.
Existing external write/delete/native replacement, parent lifetime, hardlink alias, dirty history, cancellation and no-clobber checks remain enabled in the full suite.
Legacy sidecar files and symlinks are ignored and preserved; matching suffixes are never deleted automatically.
All save and settings terminal sessions explicitly reject leftover *.vscli-write.lock or .tmp* files after shutdown.

reused_evidence.description: Host JavaScript modules are unchanged from base commit 7e39248. Its 797-test host receipt remains historical evidence and was not rerun for this native-only locking change.

limits: Cross-process writers are external; original baseline/identity checks remain but the final check-to-rename race is not excluded.
One-second bounded worker wait and 128 active resource locks are native adaptations.
Windows/macOS runtime qualification and full upstream-runtime comparison remain open.
Old sidecars remain on disk until deliberately removed after closing older instances.
